title: Cleaning up what a run leaves behind
target: How cleaning works in an R.E.P.O. level, given that cleaning has its own director and effect, that a clean spot is identified by the game, and that the level's pieces carry a clean state of their own.
prerequisites: A level you have already been through
A moment when nothing is chasing you

steps.do: Treat cleaning as a short piece of the game rather than as a menu action.
steps.because: cleaning has a director and a clean effect of its own (Clean Director, Clean Effect)

steps.do: Watch the surface rather than the tool: the sparkle is what tells you it worked.
steps.because: the clean effect is drawn from a sprite sheet of its own (Clean Effect Sprite Sheet)

steps.do: Go back over a spot the game has not registered as clean yet.
steps.because: a clean spot has an identifier of its own (Clean Spot Identifier, CleanEffectParticleSettings)

steps.do: Look for the cleaning cupboard rather than carrying everything yourself.
steps.because: the museum keeps cleaning supplies of its own, a mop among them (Museum Storage Mop, Museum Storage Cleaning Supplies)

steps.do: Expect a cleaned wall or corner to look different from an untouched one.
steps.because: the level's wall and corner pieces carry a clean version beside them (Column Bot Wall_1x0.25_Clean, Column Top Corner Wall_1x0.125_Clean)

commonMistakes: Walking past a mess because the tool is not in your hand.
Cleaning a surface the game has already marked clean instead of moving on.
Hunting for the mop in the shop when the level keeps supplies of its own.
Assuming a cleaned room means a safe one.
sources: A local copy of the game, read only. Grounding for each step is on the technical reference pages; no number is estimated.
